method: batch-005 Q-law-9: LLM close-read of the top-15 candidate pairs surfaced by collision-report-v2-005.json (_batch005-top15.json). Evidence = verbatim excerptA/excerptB text already extracted per shared paragraph in the input payload; no network fetch, no invented text -- classifications and reasoning are grounded strictly in the quoted excerpt fragments (numbers, wording, cross-references), with cross-checks limited to other excerpts already present in the same input file for the same billA (e.g. bill 4's §30 odst.1 edit visible in a sibling pair's excerpt).

pairs.reasoning: Both excerpts share the § number '35c' but land on different odstavce (billA: odst.1, the child-amount sentence; billB: odst.7, an unrelated semicolon-clause deletion) with no textual overlap or dependency visible in either excerpt. This reads as the detector matching on the bare '§ 35c' token rather than a genuine same-subsection interaction; conservatively classified incidental.
